our_title: dgraphCheck accepts out-of-range edge ends, reads past holes, checks loads only with ghosts
ran: repro/DGR-11/chk.c on the pristine ASan build (np=1,2,3; base 0/1): `far` (arc to baseval + 4P + 7) -> `check rc=0`; `hole` (arc to a hole slot of the next process, vertlocmax 4 for 2 vertices) -> `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow ... #0 _SCOTCHdgraphCheck dgraph_check.c:467`; `zero`/`neg` (symmetric non-positive loads) -> `check rc=0`; `negasym` -> only 'arc load data do not match'. Patched (np=1-4): far -> 'dgraphCheck: invalid edge array' rc=1; hole -> 'dgraphCheck: arc end in numbering hole' rc=1, no ASan; zero/neg/negasym -> 'dgraphCheck: invalid edge load' rc=1; ok -> rc=0. The same cases, added to test_scotch_dgraph_check.c, pass with -np 1-4 on 32/64/debug trees.
severity_note: Out-of-bounds read on a hand-built graph passed to the public checker and false 'valid' answers; PyScotch's test bench relies on this checker.
evidence: l.306: `if ((grafptr->flagval & DGRAPHHASEDGEGST) != 0) { /* If ghost edge array is valid */` enclosing the only `edloloctax[edgelocnum] <= 0` test (l.315-316); l.460-461: `if ((vertglbend >= vertngbmin) && (vertglbend < vertngbmax)) {` then l.466-467 `vertngbptr[vertglbend - vertngbmin]` with vertngbmax = procvrttab[procngbnum + 1] (hole included); no test of edgeloctax against the global range anywhere.
review_accuracy: accurate on all three points; its 'Fix:' line is what was done (bound by the neighbour's vertex count = proccnttab, report unmatched ends, loads unconditional).
first_pass_critique: Correct and verified. Its sketch tested ends against [baseval, procvrttab[P]) (the global range starts at procvrttab[0], which dgraphCheck never ties to baseval) and used `continue` with cheklocval = 1 for holes (reported as 'arc data do not match'); it missed that vertloctax[v] < baseval is not checked either (now in the same test as the vendloctax checks).

fix_options.label: A: range check in the local pass, hole check in the matching rounds, unconditional load check
fix_options.summary: Local pass: vertloctax >= baseval, every end in [procvrttab[0], procvrttab[P]) ('invalid edge array'), edge loads > 0, ghost checks only under DGRAPHHASEDGEGST. Matching rounds: vertngbnnd = vertngbmin + proccnttab[procngbnum]; an end at or beyond it sets error code 4 'arc end in numbering hole'.
fix_options.tested: repro/DGR-11 np=1-4 base 0/1; test_scotch_dgraph_check.c new cases (bump.grf base 0 and bump_b100000.grf base 100000) with -np 1-4 on 32/64/debug; relevant check targets: all CHECKPTSCOTCH targets (incl. the new check_scotch_dgraph_build) pass on the 32-bit ASan tree and the 64-bit tree (chk_32_summary.txt, chk_64_summary.txt; np=3 via the Makefile, plus the dgraph test programs, dgtst and dgpart with -np 1, 2 and 4); the dgraph targets pass on the -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree (chk_dbg_summary.txt). The only sanitizer hits are pre-existing ones in other groups' files (library_dgraph_coarsen.c:163 memcpy with NULL, bgraph_bipart_ml.c:195 null offset), identical to G18's logs.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Stricter: graphs with non-positive edge loads, dangling ends or ends in holes are now rejected (see notes); one compare per edge in the local pass, one per matched end in the rounds (O(E) and O(E.P) already).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Follows the file's own cheklocval/goto fail structure and message style; graphCheck (sequential) already rejects out-of-range ends ('invalid edge array') so the distributed twin now matches.

fix_options.label: B: full validation in the local pass with a binary search over procvrttab
fix_options.summary: Find the owner of each end by dichotomy (as dgraphGhst2 does) and reject hole ends there; matching rounds untouched.

ran: repro/DGR-18/grid3dfi.c (SCOTCH_dgraphBuildGrid3D 4x4x2, incrval 3 so that labels exist, then SCOTCH_dgraphExit) with fault injection on the pristine UBSan build: `scan.sh $P18/lib bin_pristinefi/grid3dfi 1 0 0 5 -- 1 3` -> nth=3: `(0): ERROR: dgraphBuild3: out of memory; signal 6 (Aborted)` (glibc double free in dgraphExit); np=2 fail rank 1: nth=3 abort, nth=0,1 HANG (grid builder's own allocation failures, PS2-G19-1), nth=2 HANG (DGR-05). Patched: np=1, np=2 fail rank 1, np=3 fail rank 2: nth=0..3 -> every rank grid3d rc=1 and exit done; nth=4,5 -> rc=0, check rc=0.
severity_note: Double free, but only on a failure inside dgraphBuild3 (label path or its consistency checks) of a test-graph generator; as the review.
evidence: l.476: `grafptr->flagval = (DGRAPHFREETABS | DGRAPHVERTGROUP | DGRAPHEDGEGROUP); /* All arrays will be freed on exit */` before l.478 `if (dgraphBuild2 (...) != 0) { memFree (datadat.edgeloctax + baseval); memFree (vertloctax + baseval); return (1); }`
first_pass_critique: Correct and verified (it even observed the nth=0,1 hangs with np>1 in its harness but filed nothing for them). Its option 2 (let dgraphExit free) is the alt diff here.

fix_options.label: A: set the flags with |= after a successful build
fix_options.summary: Move the flag assignment after dgraphBuild2 and or it, exactly like dgraphBuildHcub (dgraph_build_hcub.c:215).
fix_options.tested: fault injection nth=3 on np=1,2,3: rc=1 and clean exit; relevant check targets: all CHECKPTSCOTCH targets (incl. the new check_scotch_dgraph_build) pass on the 32-bit ASan tree and the 64-bit tree (chk_32_summary.txt, chk_64_summary.txt; np=3 via the Makefile, plus the dgraph test programs, dgtst and dgpart with -np 1, 2 and 4); the dgraph targets pass on the -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree (chk_dbg_summary.txt). The only sanitizer hits are pre-existing ones in other groups' files (library_dgraph_coarsen.c:163 memcpy with NULL, bgraph_bipart_ml.c:195 null offset), identical to G18's logs.
fix_options.tradeoffs: The failed graph keeps dangling (unflagged) pointers, as hcub/scatter/dmesh do.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: His own pattern in the sibling generator.

fix_options.label: B: keep the flags, let dgraphExit free attached arrays
fix_options.summary: Or the flags before the build and free in the routine only if grafptr->vertloctax is still NULL.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Relies on dgraphBuild3 attaching all pointers at once (true today) and on the caller calling dgraphExit; fragile.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Not his pattern; he frees what the routine allocated on its own failure.
